- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 10–15 day average is >10% above recent 30-day mean, adjust forecast downward by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying horizon adjustment.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive days >+2% from prior), model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
